samples.summary: The new `.github/workflows/ci.yml` path literal is duplicated into two workflow gates that no test pins to `CI_WORKFLOW_PATH` — a rename of ci.yml silently disables the CI-fix loop and the CI report comment
samples.evidence: The change introduces `CI_WORKFLOW_PATH` in scripts/agent/checks.mjs:58 and copies the literal into three job gates: `.github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:166`, `.github/workflows/agent-iterate-ci.yml:54`, and `.github/workflows/ci-report.yml:56`. Only the PANEL copy is pinned: `scripts/agent/checks.test.mjs:181` rewrites `github.event.workflow_run.path` to a `PATH` parameter and evaluates the panel's gate against `CI_WORKFLOW_PATH` (checks.test.mjs:193-218), so a typo there fails. Nothing evaluates the literals in agent-iterate-ci.yml:54 or ci-report.yml:56 — I grepped the whole repo for those files in tests (`scripts/agent/checks.test.mjs`, `scripts/test/ci-workflow.test.mjs`, `scripts/test/agent-workflow-guards.test.mjs`, `scripts/agent/loop-status.test.mjs`) and none of them assert the gate's path clause. The new `CI_WORKFLOW_PATH names a workflow file that actually exists` test (checks.test.mjs:443) protects the JS constant only. Consequence of drift: both gates evaluate false for every run, the CI-fix loop never fires on a red CI and ci-report never posts, with no error anywhere — exactly the silent-unsatisfiable failure the checks.test.mjs comment says it exists to prevent. Fix belongs on the new code: extend the checks.test.mjs gate-evaluation helper to the other two files.

samples.summary: The `workflows:`-filter-is-a-display-name hazard the change hardens against is left unguarded in the other three `workflow_run` consumers, one of which holds a cross-repo write token
samples.evidence: The diff hardens three of the repo's `workflow_run` consumers (agent-review-panel.yml:166, agent-iterate-ci.yml:54, ci-report.yml:56). The remaining ones still match on display name only: `.github/workflows/docker-publish.yml:67-71` and `.github/workflows/publish-ghpage.yml:42-46` (the ci-report comment argues these are covered by `head_branch == 'main' && event == 'push'`, which is a defensible mitigation), and `.github/workflows/capture-collect.yml:67-68` (`workflows: ["Agent Review Panel", "Agent Review On-Demand"]`), which the change does not mention at all. capture-collect has no branch/repo clause on its trigger (its only gate is `conclusion != 'skipped'` at capture-collect.yml:129) and checks out `dlgpdmsly2/wafflebase-agent-eval` with `secrets.EVAL_STORE_TOKEN` (capture-collect.yml:142-146), so a second workflow file merely named "Agent Review Panel" on any branch can drive that job. Impact is limited because the collector sweeps a time window rather than the triggering run, so the effect is spurious runs of a token-holding job rather than attacker-chosen data; but the guard the change adds is exactly the one missing here.

samples.summary: set-state's `ciConclusion` signal silently changed shape: it used to carry the raw run conclusion ('cancelled', 'timed_out', 'skipped'), and now only ever yields 'success' | 'failure' | null
samples.evidence: Before the change, `gatherSignals` set `sig.ciConclusion = ci.conclusion` (the raw Actions value); after it, `ciConclusion()` in scripts/agent/checks.mjs:90-93 collapses everything that is not `success` to the string `"failure"`. Today nothing breaks — `deriveState` (scripts/agent/set-state.mjs:129) only tests `=== "success"` and scripts/agent/set-state.test.mjs:83-99 only uses "success"/"failure"/null — so this is a narrowing of a value crossing a module boundary rather than a live defect. It matters because `deriveState`'s doc block (set-state.mjs:117-122) documents `ciConclusion` as one of the "unforgeable signals", and any future branch on `cancelled`/`timed_out` there will be dead code that no test would flag. Worth a one-line note on the signal's documented domain.
